content: Bisabolol, also referred to as α-(-)-bisabolol or levomenol, is a naturally occurring monocyclic sesquiterpene alcohol. It is a colorless, viscous oil that serves as the primary component of the essential oil derived from German chamomile (Matricaria recutita). This compound is nearly insoluble in water and glycerin but demonstrates good solubility in ethanol. The enantiomer of bisabolol, known as α-(+)-bisabolol, is also found in nature, though it is relatively rare. Synthetic bisabolol is typically produced as a racemic mixture, containing both enantiomers, and is referred to as α-(±)-bisabolol. Bisabolol possesses a mild, sweet, floral aroma, making it a common ingredient in various fragrances. For centuries, bisabolol has been utilized in cosmetics due to its reputed skin-healing properties. It is recognized for its anti-irritant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects, which contribute to its widespread use in skincare formulations. A structurally related compound, β-bisabolol, differs from α-bisabolol only in the position of its tertiary alcohol functional group.
